source: Phase 41 (2026-10-18): original questions on the chapters of Beast Academy Levels 1-5 and the AoPS books, written by Claude Sonnet from our own chapter summaries (docs/question-bank-beast-academy.md) and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.BA3.01: Text-only, so tested through polygon names, sides/vertices, diagonals (counts and definitions given in the stem), properties of quadrilaterals and lines of symmetry of named shapes. No figures are referred to.
notes.BA3.02: All skip-counting lists go up (or down) by a whole number; no negative numbers or fractions.
notes.BA3.03: All shapes are described in words (no figures). Notched and joined shapes state their measurements. Answers are whole numbers; products go up to 100 x 60 and 45 x 20.
notes.BA3.04: Whole-number answers only; the facts go up to 12 x 7 and 11 x 8, and a few stories multiply a one-digit number by a two-digit one. No figures: arrays are described in words.
notes.BA3.05: All text, no pictures. Squares up to 20 and 20 x 20 = 400; the four skills are recognizing square numbers, squares up to 20, differences between squares, and square arrays.
notes.BA3.06: All text. Four skills: breaking a product apart, two-digit by one-digit mentally, combining products with a common factor, missing numbers in distributive equations. A few difficulty 3 questions use a nearby-number shortcut (such as 4 x 98 from 4 x 100).
notes.BA3.07: All answers are whole numbers. Balance puzzles are written in words (pans, weights) since no picture is available. Variables are written with $...$ throughout.
notes.BA3.08: All answers are whole numbers (remainders are asked as separate whole-number questions). Division is kept to facts up to 10 x 10 (a few dozens), two-digit by one-digit, and simple tens shortcuts; nothing that needs a figure.
notes.BA3.09: All text-only; no clocks, rulers or pictures. Facts used and stated where less common: 12 inches = 1 foot, 16 ounces = 1 pound, 1000 g = 1 kg, 1000 mL = 1 liter, 60 minutes = 1 hour.
notes.BA3.10: All text-only: wholes are described in words (a pizza cut into equal slices, a bar of equal squares), no pictures or number lines. Denominators are 2 to 12 and 16 only; comparisons with different denominators use halving, doubling or twelfths.
notes.BA3.11: Ties (a number exactly halfway) are avoided in rounding questions, so no rounding-half convention is needed. Estimating questions say how to round.
notes.BA3.12: Text only: shapes made of rectangles are described by their measurements (joined, or cut from a corner), never by a picture. No fractions or decimals.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: A shape has exactly 5 straight sides. What is it called?
questions.solution: Penta- means five. A shape with 5 sides is a pentagon.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.solution: A hexagon is a polygon with 6 sides.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: Mia cuts a piece of paper into the shape of a stop sign. It has 8 straight sides. What is this shape called?
questions.solution: A polygon with 8 sides is an octagon.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: A quadrilateral is a polygon with how many sides?
questions.solution: A quadrilateral has 4 sides.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: A polygon has 3 sides and 3 corners. What do we call it?
questions.solution: A polygon with 3 sides is a triangle.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: A hexagon has 6 sides. A heptagon has 1 more side than a hexagon. How many sides does a heptagon have?
questions.solution: 6 + 1 = 7. A heptagon has 7 sides.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: Which name goes with a polygon that has 7 sides?
questions.solution: A polygon with 7 sides is a heptagon.

questions.stem: How many vertices (corners) does an octagon have?
questions.solution: A polygon has as many corners as sides. An octagon has 8 sides, so it has 8 vertices.

questions.stem: A polygon has 6 sides. How many vertices does it have?
questions.solution: A polygon always has the same number of vertices as sides, so 6.

solve.work: A polygon has as many vertices as sides: 6.

questions.stem: Two triangles lie side by side on a table and do not touch. How many sides do they have in all?
questions.solution: Each triangle has 3 sides. 3 + 3 = 6.

questions.stem: Which sentence is true for every polygon?
choices: It has more sides than vertices.
It has more vertices than sides.
It has the same number of sides as vertices.
questions.answer: It has the same number of sides as vertices.
questions.solution: In a polygon, each side ends at two corners and each corner is where two sides meet, so the number of sides equals the number of vertices.

solve.answer: It has the same number of sides as vertices.
solve.work: Every polygon has equal numbers of sides and vertices.

questions.stem: Ravi draws a square and a triangle. How many vertices do the two shapes have altogether?
questions.solution: A square has 4 vertices and a triangle has 3. 4 + 3 = 7.

questions.stem: A polygon has twice as many sides as a triangle. How many vertices does it have?
questions.solution: A triangle has 3 sides, so the polygon has 2 x 3 = 6 sides. It has 6 vertices too.

questions.stem: Dana draws a pentagon and a hexagon. Which sentence is true?
choices: The pentagon has one more vertex than the hexagon.
The hexagon has two more vertices than the pentagon.
They have the same number of vertices.
The hexagon has one more vertex than the pentagon.
questions.answer: The hexagon has one more vertex than the pentagon.
questions.solution: A pentagon has 5 vertices and a hexagon has 6, so the hexagon has 1 more.

solve.answer: The hexagon has one more vertex than the pentagon.
solve.work: Pentagon 5 vertices, hexagon 6: hexagon has one more.

questions.stem: A diagonal is a line that joins two corners that are not next to each other. How many diagonals does a square have?
questions.solution: In a square, each of the two pairs of opposite corners can be joined. That makes 2 diagonals.

solve.work: Square ABCD: AC and BD, 2 diagonals.

questions.stem: A diagonal joins two corners that are not next to each other. How many diagonals can you draw in a triangle?
questions.solution: Every corner of a triangle is next to both of the others, so a triangle has no diagonals.

solve.work: Every pair of triangle corners is adjacent, so 0 diagonals.

questions.stem: Rectangle ABCD has its corners A, B, C and D in order around it. Which line is a diagonal of the rectangle?
questions.solution: A and C are opposite corners, not next to each other, so AC is a diagonal. AB, BC and CD are sides.

solve.work: A and C are not next to each other, so AC is a diagonal; AB, BC, CD are sides.

questions.stem: Pia picks one corner of a pentagon and draws every diagonal from it. How many diagonals does she draw? (A diagonal joins two corners that are not next to each other.)
questions.solution: From one corner you cannot go to itself or to the 2 corners next to it. That leaves 5 - 3 = 2 corners.

solve.work: From one corner of 5: exclude itself and 2 neighbours: 5 - 3 = 2.

questions.stem: Jo picks one corner of a hexagon. A diagonal joins two corners that are not next to each other. How many diagonals start at that corner?
questions.solution: Leave out the corner itself and its 2 neighbors: 6 - 3 = 3 other corners to join.

questions.stem: Which sentence tells what a diagonal of a polygon is?
choices: A line that joins two corners that are next to each other
A line that joins two corners that are not next to each other
The longest side of the polygon
A line that goes around the whole polygon
questions.answer: A line that joins two corners that are not next to each other
questions.solution: A diagonal goes from one corner to another corner that is not a neighbor. A line between neighbors is a side.

solve.answer: A line that joins two corners that are not next to each other

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 sides that are all the same length and 4 square corners. Which shape is it?
questions.solution: Four equal sides and four square corners make a square.

solve.work: 4 equal sides and 4 square corners: square.

questions.stem: Which of these shapes is a quadrilateral?
questions.solution: A quadrilateral has 4 sides. A rhombus has 4 sides. The others have 5, 3 and 6.

solve.work: Rhombus has 4 sides; the others have 6, 3, 5.

questions.stem: How many square corners does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: All four corners of a rectangle are square corners.

questions.stem: Which of these quadrilaterals has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
questions.solution: A trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides. A square, rectangle and parallelogram each have two pairs.

solve.work: Square, rectangle, parallelogram have 2 pairs of parallel sides; trapezoid has exactly one pair.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a side that is 8 cm long and another side that is 5 cm long. How many of its four sides are 8 cm long?
questions.solution: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal. Two sides are 8 cm and two sides are 5 cm.

solve.work: Opposite sides equal: two sides of 8 cm and two of 5 cm, so 2.

questions.stem: Which sentence is true for every rhombus?
choices: All four corners are square corners.
All four sides are the same length.
questions.answer: All four sides are the same length.
questions.solution: A rhombus is defined by its four equal sides. Its corners need not be square.

solve.answer: All four sides are the same length.
solve.work: A rhombus has four equal sides; corners need not be square.

questions.stem: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: The two long sides are parallel, and the two short sides are parallel. That is 2 pairs.

questions.stem: A line of symmetry folds a shape into two halves that match exactly. How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.solution: A square can be folded along 2 lines through opposite corners and 2 lines through the middles of opposite sides: 4 lines.

solve.work: Square: 2 through midpoints of opposite sides + 2 diagonals = 4.

questions.stem: A rectangle is longer than it is wide. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
questions.solution: It can be folded along the line joining the middles of the long sides and along the line joining the middles of the short sides. Folding along a diagonal does not make the halves match.

solve.work: Non-square rectangle: 2 lines (through midpoints of opposite sides); diagonals are not lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: A triangle has three equal sides. In how many different ways can it be folded so the two halves match exactly?
questions.solution: Each fold goes from one corner to the middle of the opposite side. There are 3 corners, so 3 folds.

solve.work: Equilateral triangle: 3 lines of symmetry, one through each corner.

questions.stem: A regular pentagon has all sides equal and all corners equal. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
questions.solution: A regular polygon has one line of symmetry for each side, so a pentagon has 5.

questions.stem: Which shape has the most lines of symmetry?
choices: a long rectangle that is not a square
a triangle with three equal sides
a triangle with only two equal sides
questions.solution: A square has 4. The rectangle has 2, the triangle with three equal sides has 3, and the triangle with two equal sides has 1.

solve.work: Long rectangle 2, square 4, isosceles 1, equilateral 3. Most: square.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon has all sides equal and all corners equal. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
questions.solution: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides. A hexagon has 6.

questions.solution: 5 + 2 = 7, and a polygon with 7 sides is a heptagon.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: A polygon has 3 fewer sides than an octagon. How many sides does it have?
questions.solution: 8 - 3 = 5. It is a pentagon.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: A polygon has as many sides as there are days in a week. What is it called?
questions.solution: There are 7 days in a week. A polygon with 7 sides is a heptagon.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: Which list puts these shapes in order from the fewest sides to the most sides?
questions.solution: A triangle has 3 sides, a quadrilateral 4, a hexagon 6 and an octagon 8.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: Leo draws a pentagon, a hexagon and an octagon. How many sides do the three shapes have altogether?

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: Which pair names a shape with 5 sides and a shape with 6 sides?
questions.solution: A pentagon has 5 sides and a hexagon has 6.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: An octagon-shaped table has 8 sides. Pam puts one chair against each side except 2 sides that are next to a wall. How many chairs does she use?
questions.solution: 8 - 2 = 6 chairs.

questions.stem: A triangle and another polygon have 9 vertices altogether. How many sides does the other polygon have?
questions.solution: The triangle has 3 vertices. 9 - 3 = 6, so the other polygon has 6 vertices and 6 sides.

questions.stem: Kim draws three separate squares. How many vertices do the squares have altogether?
questions.solution: Each square has 4 vertices. 3 x 4 = 12.

questions.stem: A polygon has 8 vertices. Which sentence must be true?
questions.solution: A polygon has as many sides as vertices, so it has 8 sides.

questions.stem: Two polygons have 11 sides altogether. One of them is a pentagon. How many vertices does the other polygon have?
questions.solution: 11 - 5 = 6 sides for the other polygon, so it has 6 vertices.

questions.stem: Lena puts a dot at each corner of two hexagons and one square. How many dots does she draw?
Which group of shapes has the most vertices?
questions.solution: Two pentagons have 10 vertices. Three triangles have 9, two squares have 8 and a heptagon has 7.

solve.work: Three triangles 9, two squares 8, two pentagons 10, heptagon 7. Most: two pentagons.

questions.stem: A hexagon has 6 sides and 6 vertices. How many sides and vertices does it have if you count them together?
questions.solution: Count 6 sides and 6 vertices: 6 + 6 = 12.

questions.stem: A diagonal is a line that joins two corners that are not next to each other. A pentagon has 5 diagonals. A hexagon has 9. How many more diagonals does a hexagon have than a pentagon?
How many diagonals start at one corner of a heptagon? (A diagonal joins two corners that are not next to each other.)
questions.solution: Leave out the corner itself and its 2 neighbors: 7 - 3 = 4.

questions.stem: Which polygon has no diagonals at all?
questions.solution: In a triangle every pair of corners is already next to each other. All the others have diagonals.

solve.work: Triangle: all corners adjacent, no diagonals.

questions.stem: Quadrilateral PQRS has its corners P, Q, R and S in order around it. Which two lines are its diagonals?
questions.solution: P and R are opposite corners and so are Q and S, so PR and QS are the diagonals. The others are sides.

questions.stem: A hexagon has 6 sides and 9 diagonals. Tess draws all the sides and all the diagonals. How many lines does she draw?
The diagonals of a square are drawn. Which sentence is true?
choices: They are parallel to each other.
They cross each other inside the square.
They are the same as two sides.
questions.answer: They cross each other inside the square.
questions.solution: The two diagonals of a square join opposite corners and cross in the middle. A square has 2 diagonals.

solve.answer: They cross each other inside the square.
solve.work: Diagonals of a square cross at the centre; there are 2, not parallel, not sides.

questions.stem: Which sentence is true for every rectangle?
choices: It has exactly one pair of parallel sides.
All four corners are square corners.
questions.answer: All four corners are square corners.
questions.solution: Every rectangle has four square corners. Only some rectangles have four equal sides.

solve.answer: All four corners are square corners.
solve.work: Every rectangle has 4 square corners; it has 2 pairs of parallel sides; sides need not all be equal.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has four equal sides and two pairs of parallel sides. Its corners are slanted, not square. Which shape is it?
questions.solution: Four equal sides with slanted corners make a rhombus. A rectangle and a square have square corners.

solve.work: Four equal sides, slanted corners: rhombus.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has two pairs of equal sides that touch each other. The opposite sides are not equal. Which shape is it?
questions.solution: That is a kite. In a rectangle or parallelogram the opposite sides are equal.

solve.work: Two pairs of equal adjacent sides, opposite sides unequal: kite.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has three sides that are 7 cm, 4 cm and 7 cm long, in that order around the shape. How long is the fourth side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal. The sides in order are 7, 4, 7 and the last must match the 4.

solve.work: Opposite sides of a parallelogram equal: sides 7, 4, 7, 4. Fourth = 4.

questions.stem: Which sentence is true?
questions.solution: A square has four square corners, so it is a rectangle. A rectangle with unequal sides is not a square.

solve.work: A square has 4 square corners, so it is a rectangle. Others false.

questions.stem: A rhombus has one side that is 5 cm long. What is the sum of the lengths of all four of its sides, in centimeters?
questions.solution: All four sides of a rhombus are equal. 4 x 5 = 20.

questions.stem: Which group names only quadrilaterals?
questions.solution: Every shape in the correct group has 4 sides. The others each include a triangle, a pentagon or a hexagon.

solve.work: Square, rhombus, trapezoid all 4-sided; the other lists contain a pentagon, hexagon or triangle.

questions.stem: A slanted parallelogram has two long sides, two short sides and no square corners. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
questions.solution: No fold makes the two halves match, so it has no lines of symmetry.

solve.work: A slanted non-rhombus parallelogram has 0 lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: A rhombus has four equal sides but its corners are not square. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
questions.solution: It can be folded along each of its two diagonals so that the halves match. Those are its 2 lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: A triangle has two sides of equal length and a third side that is different. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
questions.solution: The only fold that works goes from the corner between the two equal sides to the middle of the opposite side.

questions.stem: Which shape has exactly 1 line of symmetry?
choices: a triangle with exactly two equal sides
a rectangle that is not a square
questions.answer: a triangle with exactly two equal sides
questions.solution: The triangle has 1. The rectangle has 2, the square has 4 and the slanted parallelogram has 0.

solve.answer: a triangle with exactly two equal sides
solve.work: Parallelogram 0, isosceles triangle 1, square 4, rectangle 2. Exactly 1: isosceles.

questions.stem: A regular polygon has 7 lines of symmetry. How many sides does it have?
questions.solution: A regular polygon has one line of symmetry for each side.

solve.work: A regular n-gon has n lines: 7.

questions.stem: Which shape has more lines of symmetry than a rectangle that is not a square?
choices: a triangle with three equal sides
a triangle with exactly two equal sides
a kite that is not a rhombus
questions.answer: a triangle with three equal sides
questions.solution: The rectangle has 2. The triangle with three equal sides has 3. The others have 0, 1 and 1.

solve.answer: a triangle with three equal sides
solve.work: Rectangle has 2. Kite 1, isosceles 1, parallelogram 0, equilateral triangle 3. Answer: equilateral.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: Two polygons have 13 sides altogether. One of them is a hexagon. What is the other one called?
questions.solution: 13 - 6 = 7 sides, so the other polygon is a heptagon.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: A hexagon, an octagon and one more polygon have 20 sides altogether. How many sides does the third polygon have?
questions.solution: 6 + 8 = 14 sides so far. 20 - 14 = 6.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: Eli has a triangle, a quadrilateral, a pentagon and a hexagon. Which one has exactly 2 more sides than the triangle?
questions.solution: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 + 2 = 5, so it is the pentagon.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: A polygon has 4 fewer sides than an octagon and 1 more side than a triangle. What is it called?
questions.solution: 8 - 4 = 4 and 3 + 1 = 4. A polygon with 4 sides is a quadrilateral.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: Liv has a pentagon, a heptagon and a quadrilateral. How many sides does the one with the middle number of sides have?
questions.solution: The sides are 5, 7 and 4. In order: 4, 5, 7. The middle one is 5.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: Add together the number of sides of a triangle, a quadrilateral, a pentagon, a hexagon, a heptagon and an octagon.

questions.skill: Naming polygons by number of sides
questions.stem: A hexagon has twice as many sides as a triangle. Which polygon has twice as many sides as a quadrilateral?
questions.solution: 2 x 4 = 8, and a polygon with 8 sides is an octagon.

questions.stem: Ned draws a square, a pentagon and a heptagon. How many vertices do the three shapes have altogether?
A polygon has 5 more vertices than a triangle. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.solution: A triangle has 3 vertices. 3 + 5 = 8 vertices, so 8 sides.

questions.stem: Some triangles are drawn apart from each other. Together they have 15 vertices. How many triangles are there?
questions.solution: Each triangle has 3 vertices. 15 / 3 = 5.

questions.stem: Hal draws 2 squares and some triangles, all apart from each other. The shapes have 17 vertices in all. How many triangles did he draw?
questions.solution: The squares have 2 x 4 = 8 vertices. The triangles have 17 - 8 = 9 vertices. 9 / 3 = 3 triangles.

questions.stem: Which pair of polygons has 11 sides altogether?
questions.solution: 5 + 6 = 11. The other pairs make 9, 10 and 12.

questions.stem: A square piece of paper has one corner cut off with a single straight cut that goes from one side to the next side and does not touch any other corner. How many sides does the new shape have?
questions.solution: The cut removes one corner and adds a new side. The 2 sides that met at the corner are shorter but still there. 4 + 1 = 5 sides.

solve.work: Cutting one corner replaces 1 vertex with 2: 4 + 1 = 5 sides.

questions.stem: One corner of a triangle is cut off with a single straight cut from one side to the next side. What is the new shape called?
questions.solution: The cut adds one new side, so there are 3 + 1 = 4 sides. A polygon with 4 sides is a quadrilateral.

questions.stem: How many diagonals does a hexagon have? (A diagonal joins two corners that are not next to each other.) Hint: 3 diagonals start at each corner, and each diagonal has two ends.
questions.solution: 6 corners x 3 diagonals each = 18, but every diagonal was counted from both ends. 18 / 2 = 9.

questions.stem: From each corner of an octagon, 5 diagonals can be drawn. Each diagonal has two ends, so counting corner by corner counts every diagonal twice. How many diagonals does an octagon have?
questions.solution: 8 x 5 = 40, and each diagonal was counted twice. 40 / 2 = 20.

questions.stem: How many diagonals does a heptagon have? (A diagonal joins two corners that are not next to each other.)
questions.solution: From each of the 7 corners, 7 - 3 = 4 diagonals start. 7 x 4 = 28, but each diagonal is counted twice. 28 / 2 = 14.

questions.stem: From one corner of a polygon, 5 diagonals can be drawn. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.solution: The diagonals go to every corner except the corner itself and its 2 neighbors. So there are 5 + 3 = 8 corners.

questions.stem: All the diagonals from one corner of a hexagon are drawn. They cut the hexagon into triangles. How many triangles are there?
questions.solution: Three diagonals start at the corner. Three lines cut the shape into 3 + 1 = 4 pieces, and each piece is a triangle.

solve.work: 3 diagonals from one corner split the hexagon into 4 triangles (n - 2).

questions.stem: A polygon has exactly 9 diagonals. Which polygon is it?
questions.solution: A pentagon has 5 diagonals, a hexagon has 9, a heptagon has 14 and an octagon has 20.

questions.stem: Which sentence is false?
questions.solution: A rhombus can have slanted corners, so it is not always a square. The other three sentences are true.

solve.work: A rhombus need not have square corners, so "Every rhombus is a square" is false; others true.

questions.stem: A square is cut along both of its diagonals. How many triangles are made?
questions.solution: The two diagonals cross in the middle and cut the square into 4 triangles.

solve.work: Both diagonals cut a square into 4 triangles.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has two sides of 3 cm and two sides of 8 cm. What is the total length of all four sides, in centimeters?
A rectangle is 3 cm wide and 7 cm long. A square 3 cm by 3 cm is cut off one end. What is left?
questions.solution: The length goes from 7 cm to 7 - 3 = 4 cm. The width is still 3 cm, so a 3 cm by 4 cm rectangle is left.

solve.work: 7 - 3 = 4: a 3 cm by 4 cm rectangle remains.

questions.stem: A square is cut into two equal rectangles by a straight cut through the middles of two opposite sides. How many sides do the two rectangles have altogether?
questions.solution: Each rectangle has 4 sides. 2 x 4 = 8.

questions.stem: A kite has two pairs of equal sides. One pair is 5 cm long and the other pair is 9 cm long. What is the total length of all four sides, in centimeters?
Zoe says: "My shape has 4 sides. Opposite sides are equal and parallel. The corners are not square and the sides are not all equal." What is her shape?
questions.solution: Opposite sides equal and parallel gives a parallelogram. A rhombus would have four equal sides and a rectangle would have square corners.

solve.work: Opposite sides equal and parallel, corners not square, sides not all equal: parallelogram.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry do a square and a triangle with three equal sides have altogether?
questions.solution: The square has 4 and the triangle has 3. 4 + 3 = 7.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry do a regular hexagon and a regular pentagon have altogether?
questions.solution: A hexagon has 6 and a pentagon has 5. 6 + 5 = 11.

questions.stem: A triangle has 3 lines of symmetry. Which sentence must be true about its sides?
choices: Exactly two sides are the same length.
No two sides are the same length.
All three sides are the same length.
questions.answer: All three sides are the same length.
questions.solution: Only a triangle with three equal sides can be folded in 3 different ways so the halves match.

solve.answer: All three sides are the same length.
solve.work: 3 lines of symmetry means equilateral: all sides equal.

questions.stem: A shape has exactly 2 lines of symmetry. Which shape could it be?
choices: a rectangle that is longer than it is wide
a triangle with three equal sides
a kite that is not a rhombus
questions.answer: a rectangle that is longer than it is wide
questions.solution: A long rectangle has 2. A regular pentagon has 5, the triangle has 3, and the kite has 1.

solve.answer: a rectangle that is longer than it is wide
solve.work: Regular pentagon 5, equilateral 3, non-square rectangle 2, kite 1. Rectangle.

questions.stem: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as 2 triangles have vertices altogether. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.solution: 2 triangles have 2 x 3 = 6 vertices. The polygon has 6 lines of symmetry, so 6 sides.

solve.work: 2 triangles have 6 vertices; regular polygon with 6 lines has 6 sides.
