questions.stem: A coach has 72 players and makes teams of 8 players. Each field is used by 3 teams. How many fields are needed?
questions.solution: $72 \div 8 = 9$ teams. $9 \div 3 = 3$ fields.

questions.stem: A bakery makes 100 buns and packs them in boxes of 12. Only full boxes are made. How many buns are left over?
questions.solution: $8 \times 12 = 96$ and $9 \times 12 = 108$ is too many. $100 - 96 = 4$ buns are left over.

questions.stem: When a number is divided by 6, the remainder is 4. Which number could it be?
questions.solution: $34 = 5 \times 6 + 4$. The others leave remainders 0, 5 and 3.

questions.stem: Pens come in boxes of 8. A school needs 83 pens. What is the smallest number of boxes it can buy?
questions.solution: $83 \div 8 = 10$ remainder 3. 10 boxes hold only 80 pens, so the school needs 11 boxes.

questions.stem: Which division has the greatest remainder?
questions.solution: The remainders are: $29 \div 10$ leaves 9; $29 \div 6$ leaves 5; $29 \div 7$ leaves 1; $29 \div 5$ leaves 4. The greatest is 9.

questions.stem: Divide 59 by 8. What is the quotient plus the remainder?
questions.solution: $7 \times 8 = 56$ and $59 - 56 = 3$. The quotient is 7 and the remainder is 3, so the total is $7 + 3 = 10$.

questions.stem: A pattern of beads repeats red, blue, green, yellow over and over. What color is the 50th bead?
questions.solution: Each group of 4 beads uses the colors once. $50 \div 4 = 12$ remainder 2, so the 50th bead is the 2nd color in a group: blue.

questions.stem: A number is divided by 7. The quotient is 8 and the remainder is 5. What is the number?
What is the largest whole number less than 100 that leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 8?
questions.solution: $12 \times 8 = 96$, and $96 + 3 = 99$ is less than 100. The next number that works, 107, is too big. So the answer is 99.

questions.stem: A number between 10 and 30 leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 4 and a remainder of 2 when divided by 5. What is the number?
questions.solution: Numbers between 10 and 30 that leave remainder 1 when divided by 4 are 13, 17, 21, 25 and 29. Only 17 leaves remainder 2 when divided by 5 ($17 = 3 \times 5 + 2$).

questions.stem: How many different numbers of friends from 2 to 12 can share 24 cookies equally with none left over?
questions.solution: The numbers from 2 to 12 that divide 24 are 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12. That is 6 numbers.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 50 can be divided by 7 with no remainder?
questions.solution: These are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 and 49, which is 7 numbers. (Also $50 \div 7 = 7$ remainder 1.)

questions.skill: Division as the opposite of multiplication
questions.stem: $? \div 4 + 3 = 11$. What number goes in place of ?
questions.solution: Undo the steps in reverse. $11 - 3 = 8$. Then $8 \times 4 = 32$. Check: $32 \div 4 + 3 = 11$.

questions.skill: Division as the opposite of multiplication
questions.stem: Two numbers multiply to 72. One of them is 8. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution: The other number is $72 \div 8 = 9$. The sum is $8 + 9 = 17$.

questions.skill: Division as the opposite of multiplication
questions.stem: A number times 6 is the same as 3 times 24. What is the number?

questions.skill: Division as the opposite of multiplication
questions.stem: What number goes in place of ? to make $96 \div ? = 4 \times 2$ true?

questions.skill: Division stories with more than one step
questions.stem: A farmer has 5 pens with 8 sheep in each pen. He sells 12 sheep. The rest go equally into 4 trucks. How many sheep are in each truck?
questions.solution: $5 \times 8 = 40$ sheep. $40 - 12 = 28$ are left. $28 \div 4 = 7$ sheep per truck.

questions.skill: Division stories with more than one step
questions.stem: A book has 100 pages. Pam reads 8 pages each day, and her last day may be a shorter one. How many days does it take her to finish the book?
questions.solution: $100 \div 8 = 12$ remainder 4. 12 days cover 96 pages, and the last 4 pages need one more day. So 13 days.

questions.skill: Division stories with more than one step
questions.stem: A teacher has 47 crayons. Each box holds 5 crayons. How many more crayons does she need to fill one more box completely?
questions.solution: $47 \div 5 = 9$ remainder 2. The extra 2 crayons are in a box that needs 5, so she needs $5 - 2 = 3$ more.

questions.skill: Division stories with more than one step
questions.stem: Two bags hold 29 marbles and 20 marbles. The marbles from both bags are put together and then made into piles of 6. How many marbles are left over?
questions.solution: $29 + 20 = 49$ marbles. $49 \div 6 = 8$ remainder 1, since $8 \times 6 = 48$. So 1 marble is left over.

questions.skill: Division stories with more than one step
questions.stem: A pack of 6 pencils costs 3 dollars. How many dollars do 48 pencils cost?
questions.solution: $48 \div 6 = 8$ packs. Each pack costs 3 dollars, so $8 \times 3 = 24$ dollars.

questions.skill: Division stories with more than one step
questions.stem: A hall has 8 rows with 9 chairs in each row. The chairs are stacked in piles of 4. How many piles are there?
questions.solution: $8 \times 9 = 72$ chairs. $72 \div 4 = 18$ piles.

questions.stem: Three friends share some stickers equally. Each friend gets 8 stickers and 2 stickers are left over. How many stickers were there?
questions.solution: 3 friends with 8 each use $3 \times 8 = 24$ stickers. Adding the 2 left over: $24 + 2 = 26$.

questions.stem: I am a number less than 50. When I am divided by 6 the remainder is 5. When I am divided by 7 the remainder is 6. What number am I?
questions.solution: Numbers below 50 that leave remainder 5 when divided by 6 are 5, 11, 17, 23, 29, 35, 41, 47. Of these, only 41 leaves remainder 6 when divided by 7 ($41 = 5 \times 7 + 6$).

solve.work: One less than a multiple of 6 and of 7, i.e. of 42: 41 (next 83).

questions.stem: Which has the greatest quotient?
questions.solution: $60 \div 5 = 12$, $60 \div 6 = 10$, $72 \div 8 = 9$ and $90 \div 9 = 10$. The greatest is 12.

questions.stem: A ribbon is 3 feet long. There are 12 inches in 1 foot. How many inches long is the ribbon?
questions.solution: Each foot is 12 inches, so 3 feet is $3 \times 12 = 36$ inches.

questions.stem: Which is the longest length?
questions.solution: Change each to inches (12 inches in a foot): 2 feet is 24 inches, 1 foot 6 inches is 18 inches. So 30 inches is the longest.

solve.work: 1 ft 6 in = 18 in; 20 in; 30 in; 2 ft = 24 in. Longest is 30 inches.

questions.stem: A rope measures 48 inches. How many feet is that? (1 foot is 12 inches.)
questions.solution: Count groups of 12 inches: $48 \div 12 = 4$ feet.

questions.stem: A board is 2 feet 5 inches long. How long is it in inches?
questions.solution: 2 feet is $2 \times 12 = 24$ inches. Add the 5 extra inches: $24 + 5 = 29$ inches.

questions.stem: Which length is the same as 60 inches?
questions.solution: Every 12 inches make 1 foot. $60 \div 12 = 5$, so 60 inches is 5 feet.

questions.stem: A loaf of bread weighs 2 pounds. There are 16 ounces in 1 pound. How many ounces does the loaf weigh?
questions.solution: $2 \times 16 = 32$ ounces.

questions.stem: There are 16 ounces in 1 pound. Which weight is the greatest?
questions.solution: 1 pound is 16 ounces. Comparing 20, 16, 12 and 15 ounces, 20 ounces is the most.

questions.stem: A bag of rice weighs 48 ounces. How many pounds is that? (16 ounces make 1 pound.)
questions.solution: $48 \div 16 = 3$ pounds.

questions.stem: A bag of flour weighs 2 kilograms. There are 1000 grams in 1 kilogram. How many grams does the bag weigh?
questions.solution: $2 \times 1000 = 2000$ grams.

questions.stem: An apple weighs 150 grams and a pear weighs 120 grams. How many grams do they weigh together?
A watermelon weighs 5000 grams. How many kilograms is that?
questions.solution: $5000 \div 1000 = 5$ kilograms.

questions.stem: Which is the best guess for the weight of one paper clip?
questions.solution: A paper clip is very light. About 1 gram is right; the others are far too heavy.

solve.work: A paper clip weighs about 1 gram.

questions.stem: Which weight is the same as 3 kilograms?
questions.solution: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams, so 3 kilograms is $3 \times 1000 = 3000$ grams.

questions.stem: A jug holds 3 liters. There are 1000 milliliters (mL) in 1 liter. How many milliliters does the jug hold?
A pot holds 9 liters of soup. A cook uses 3 liters. How many liters of soup are left?
questions.solution: $9 - 3 = 6$ liters.

questions.stem: Which of these holds the most water?
questions.solution: A bathtub holds far more than a bucket, a mug or a teaspoon.

solve.work: A bathtub holds by far the most.

questions.stem: A tank holds 4000 mL of water. How many liters is that?
questions.solution: Every 1000 mL is 1 liter. $4000 \div 1000 = 4$ liters.

questions.stem: About how much water does a full cup hold?
questions.solution: A cup holds about a quarter of a liter, which is 250 mL. The other amounts are much too big.

questions.stem: A movie is 2 hours long. How many minutes is that? (1 hour is 60 minutes.)
questions.solution: $2 \times 60 = 120$ minutes.

questions.stem: A bus trip takes 180 minutes. How many hours is that?
questions.solution: $180 \div 60 = 3$ hours.

questions.stem: Which length of time is the same as 90 minutes?
questions.solution: 60 minutes make 1 hour, and $90 - 60 = 30$ minutes are left over: 1 hour 30 minutes.

questions.stem: A music lesson is 1 hour 15 minutes long. How many minutes is that?
A game starts at 3:00 and ends at 5:00 on the same afternoon. How many hours does it last?
questions.solution: From 3:00 to 5:00 is 2 hours.

questions.stem: Lunch starts at 12:15 and ends at 12:45. How many minutes long is lunch?
School starts at 8:00 in the morning and ends at 3:00 in the afternoon. How many hours long is the school day?
questions.solution: From 8:00 to 12:00 is 4 hours, and 12:00 to 3:00 is 3 more hours. $4 + 3 = 7$ hours.

solve.work: 8:00 AM to 12:00 = 4 h, 12:00 to 3:00 PM = 3 h; total 7 hours.

questions.stem: A bus leaves at 4:10 and arrives at 4:50. How many minutes does the trip take?
A class starts at 9:30 and lasts 1 hour. At what time does it end?
questions.solution: One hour after 9:30 is 10:30.

questions.stem: A cake goes into the oven at 4:00 and bakes for 45 minutes. At what time does it come out?
questions.solution: 45 minutes after 4:00 is 4:45.

questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring how heavy a bicycle is?
questions.solution: Weight is measured in pounds (or ounces). Inches measure length, liters measure capacity and minutes measure time.

questions.stem: Which unit would you use to measure how long a classroom is?
questions.solution: Length is measured in units like feet. Pounds measure weight, liters measure capacity and hours measure time.

questions.stem: Which unit would you use to measure how much water a bucket holds?
questions.solution: The amount a bucket holds is its capacity, measured in liters.

questions.stem: About how long does it take to brush your teeth?
questions.solution: Brushing teeth takes about 2 minutes. Hours or days are far too long.

questions.stem: A pencil is 7 inches long. Two of these pencils are laid end to end. How many inches long are they together?
questions.solution: $7 + 7 = 14$ inches.

questions.stem: Dev has a jump rope that is 7 feet long. He cuts off 20 inches. How many inches of rope are left?
questions.solution: 7 feet is $7 \times 12 = 84$ inches. Then $84 - 20 = 64$ inches are left.

questions.stem: Which length is equal to 3 feet 9 inches?
questions.solution: 3 feet is 36 inches. Adding 9 more inches gives $36 + 9 = 45$ inches.

questions.stem: A shelf is 5 feet long. Each book on it is 2 inches thick, and the books fill the shelf exactly with no gaps. How many books are on the shelf?
questions.solution: The shelf is $5 \times 12 = 60$ inches long. $60 \div 2 = 30$ books fit.

questions.stem: A plank is 100 inches long. How many feet and inches is that?
questions.solution: $8 \times 12 = 96$, which is 4 less than 100. So the plank is 8 feet 4 inches.

questions.stem: One ribbon is 2 feet 8 inches long and another is 1 foot 9 inches long. They are laid end to end. How many inches long are they together?
questions.solution: The first is 32 inches and the second is 21 inches. $32 + 21 = 53$ inches.

solve.work: 2 ft 8 in = 32 in; 1 ft 9 in = 21 in; 32 + 21 = 53 inches.

questions.stem: A cat weighs 9 pounds 4 ounces. How many ounces is that? (16 ounces make 1 pound.)
questions.solution: 9 pounds is $9 \times 16 = 144$ ounces. Add 4 more ounces: 148 ounces.

questions.stem: Box A weighs 3 pounds. Box B weighs 40 ounces. There are 16 ounces in 1 pound. How many more ounces does the heavier box weigh than the lighter one?
questions.solution: Box A is 48 ounces. Box B is 40 ounces. $48 - 40 = 8$ ounces.

questions.stem: Which weight is equal to 70 ounces? (16 ounces make 1 pound.)
questions.solution: 4 pounds is 64 ounces. $70 - 64 = 6$, so 70 ounces is 4 pounds 6 ounces.

questions.stem: A cook uses 4 blocks of butter. Each block weighs 8 ounces. How many pounds of butter is that? (16 ounces make 1 pound.)
questions.solution: $4 \times 8 = 32$ ounces, and $32 \div 16 = 2$ pounds.

questions.stem: A parcel weighs 3 kilograms 250 grams. How many grams is that?
questions.solution: 3 kilograms is 3000 grams. $3000 + 250 = 3250$ grams.

questions.stem: Which weight is equal to 4500 grams?
questions.solution: 4000 grams is 4 kilograms, and 500 grams are left over: 4 kilograms 500 grams.

questions.stem: A crate holds 8 bags of sand. Each bag weighs 250 grams. How many kilograms of sand are in the crate?
questions.solution: $8 \times 250 = 2000$ grams, which is 2 kilograms.

questions.stem: A suitcase may weigh at most 20 kilograms. Mara's suitcase weighs 14 kilograms 500 grams. How many more grams can she add without going over?
questions.solution: 20 kilograms is 20000 grams and her suitcase is 14500 grams. $20000 - 14500 = 5500$ grams.

questions.stem: A bucket holds 12 liters. A jug holds 2 liters. How many full jugs of water does it take to fill the bucket?
questions.solution: $12 \div 2 = 6$ jugs.

questions.stem: Which amount is equal to 2 liters 300 mL?
questions.solution: 2 liters is 2000 mL. Adding 300 mL gives 2300 mL.

questions.stem: Tom fills a 10 liter tank using a cup that holds 500 mL. How many cups of water does he pour in?
questions.solution: The tank holds 10000 mL. $10000 \div 500 = 20$ cups.

questions.stem: A bottle holds 750 mL. How many liters of water are in 4 full bottles?
questions.solution: $4 \times 750 = 3000$ mL, which is 3 liters.

questions.stem: Which is the greatest amount?
questions.solution: In mL the choices are 1100, 1000 and 900 against 1500. The greatest is 1500 mL.

questions.stem: How many glasses of 250 mL can be filled completely from a 3 liter jug?
questions.solution: 3 liters is 3000 mL, and $3000 \div 250 = 12$ glasses.

questions.stem: Kia practices the piano for 25 minutes every day for 6 days. How long is that in all?
questions.solution: $25 \times 6 = 150$ minutes. 150 minutes is 2 hours (120 minutes) and 30 minutes.

questions.stem: A show lasts 135 minutes. That is 2 hours and how many more minutes?
questions.solution: 2 hours is 120 minutes. $135 - 120 = 15$ minutes.

questions.stem: Which is the longest length of time?
questions.solution: In minutes: 2 hours = 120, 1 hour 50 minutes = 110, 100, and 130. The longest is 130 minutes.

questions.stem: Each song on a playlist lasts 4 minutes. The playlist plays for exactly 2 hours. How many songs are on it?
questions.solution: 2 hours is 120 minutes. $120 \div 4 = 30$ songs.

questions.stem: Liam reads for 40 minutes every night for 6 nights. How many hours does he read in all?
questions.solution: $40 \times 6 = 240$ minutes. $240 \div 60 = 4$ hours.

questions.stem: A timer is set for 95 minutes. How many minutes is that more than 1 hour?
A train leaves at 7:45 and arrives at 9:15. How many minutes does the trip take?
questions.solution: From 7:45 to 8:45 is 60 minutes, and from 8:45 to 9:15 is 30 more. $60 + 30 = 90$ minutes.

questions.stem: A play begins at 6:50 PM and ends at 8:20 PM. How long is the play?
questions.solution: 6:50 to 7:50 is 1 hour, then 7:50 to 8:20 is 30 minutes. In all: 1 hour 30 minutes.

questions.stem: Rita starts a puzzle at 2:25 and finishes at 4:10. How many minutes does she take?
questions.solution: 2:25 to 4:25 is 120 minutes, which is 15 too many. $120 - 15 = 105$ minutes.

questions.stem: A swimming lesson starts at 4:30 and lasts 50 minutes. At what time does it end?
questions.solution: 4:30 plus 30 minutes is 5:00, plus 20 more minutes is 5:20.

questions.stem: A movie ended at 8:15 and was 2 hours 30 minutes long. At what time did it start?
questions.solution: Go back 2 hours from 8:15 to 6:15, then back 30 more minutes to 5:45.

questions.stem: A lesson starts at 1:40 and ends at 2:25. How many minutes long is the lesson?
questions.solution: 1:40 to 2:00 is 20 minutes, and 2:00 to 2:25 is 25 minutes. $20 + 25 = 45$ minutes.

questions.stem: Mom mixes 2 pounds of flour with 12 ounces of sugar in one big bowl. How many ounces of mix are in the bowl? (16 ounces make 1 pound.)
questions.solution: 2 pounds is 32 ounces. $32 + 12 = 44$ ounces.

questions.stem: Only one of these comparisons is correct. Which one?
questions.solution: 2 liters is 2000 mL, which is more than 1500 mL. 3 feet is 36 inches, 1 hour is 60 minutes and 1 kilogram is 1000 grams, so the other statements are false.

questions.stem: A fence is made of 8 boards laid end to end. Each board is 18 inches long. How many feet long is the whole fence?
questions.solution: $8 \times 18 = 144$ inches, and $144 \div 12 = 12$ feet.

questions.stem: A snail crawls 6 inches every minute. How far does it crawl in 20 minutes?
questions.solution: $6 \times 20 = 120$ inches. $120 \div 12 = 10$ feet.

questions.stem: A rope is 10 feet long. Tia cuts off 3 pieces, each 2 feet 6 inches long. How many inches of rope are left?
questions.solution: The rope is 120 inches. Each piece is 30 inches, so the 3 pieces use 90 inches. $120 - 90 = 30$ inches are left.

solve.work: 10 ft = 120 in; each piece 30 in, 3 pieces 90 in; 120 - 90 = 30 inches.

questions.stem: Which statement about 5 feet 10 inches is true?
choices: 5 feet 10 inches is equal to 510 inches.
5 feet 10 inches is less than 5 feet 8 inches.
5 feet 10 inches is more than 6 feet.
5 feet 10 inches is equal to 70 inches.
questions.answer: 5 feet 10 inches is equal to 70 inches.
questions.solution: 5 feet is 60 inches, and 60 + 10 = 70 inches. The other statements are false.

solve.answer: 5 feet 10 inches is equal to 70 inches.
solve.work: 5 ft 10 in = 60 + 10 = 70 in; the other statements are false.

questions.stem: Jo cut 3 equal pieces from a board, each 16 inches long. Exactly 1 foot of the board was left over. How many feet long was the board at the start?
questions.solution: The pieces use $3 \times 16 = 48$ inches. Add the 12 inches left: $48 + 12 = 60$ inches, which is 5 feet.

solve.work: 3 x 16 = 48 in, + 12 in left = 60 in = 5 feet.

questions.stem: Eli puts 5 books into an empty bag. Each book weighs 12 ounces and the bag weighs 4 ounces. How many pounds does the bag with the books weigh? (16 ounces make 1 pound.)
questions.solution: The books weigh $5 \times 12 = 60$ ounces. With the bag: 64 ounces. $64 \div 16 = 4$ pounds.

questions.stem: A melon weighs 2 pounds 6 ounces and a pineapple weighs 2 pounds 14 ounces. How much do they weigh together? (16 ounces make 1 pound.)
questions.solution: Pounds: 2 + 2 = 4. Ounces: 6 + 14 = 20, which is 1 pound 4 ounces. So the total is 5 pounds 4 ounces.

solve.work: 4 lb + 20 oz = 4 lb + 1 lb 4 oz = 5 pounds 4 ounces.

questions.stem: A box with 4 equal books inside weighs 7 pounds 4 ounces. The empty box weighs 4 ounces. How many ounces does one book weigh? (16 ounces make 1 pound.)
questions.solution: Without the box the books weigh 7 pounds, or $7 \times 16 = 112$ ounces. $112 \div 4 = 28$ ounces each.

solve.work: 7 lb 4 oz = 116 oz; minus box 4 = 112; / 4 = 28 ounces.

questions.stem: Which of these weighs the most? (16 ounces make 1 pound.)
questions.solution: Change all to ounces: 3 pounds = 48, 2 pounds 12 ounces = 44, 47 and 50. The greatest is 50 ounces.

solve.work: 3 lb = 48 oz; 50; 47; 2 lb 12 oz = 44. Most: 50 ounces.

questions.stem: Box A and box B weigh the same. Together they weigh 3 kilograms 400 grams. Box C weighs 900 grams less than box A. How many grams does box C weigh?
questions.solution: Together 3400 grams, so each of A and B is $3400 \div 2 = 1700$ grams. Box C: $1700 - 900 = 800$ grams.

questions.stem: Which of these weighs the most?
questions.solution: In grams: 2050, 2005 and 1999 against 2500. The largest is 2500 grams.

questions.stem: One melon weighs the same as 4 apples. Each apple weighs 350 grams. Ben puts 2 melons and a 600 gram box on a scale. How many grams does the scale show?
questions.solution: A melon is $4 \times 350 = 1400$ grams. Two melons are 2800 grams. Add the box: $2800 + 600 = 3400$ grams.

questions.stem: A pitcher holds 2 liters of juice. Sam pours 250 mL into each of 6 cups. How many mL are left in the pitcher?
questions.solution: The cups take $6 \times 250 = 1500$ mL. $2000 - 1500 = 500$ mL are left.

questions.stem: Five equal bottles hold 3 liters 500 mL of water in all. How many mL does one bottle hold?
questions.solution: 3 liters 500 mL is 3500 mL. $3500 \div 5 = 700$ mL.

questions.stem: A tank holds 6 liters of water. 1 liter 400 mL leaks out, then 800 mL is poured in. How much water is in the tank now?
questions.solution: 6000 - 1400 = 4600 mL, then 4600 + 800 = 5400 mL, which is 5 liters 400 mL.

questions.stem: A jug had some water. After 1 liter 200 mL was poured out, 800 mL was left. How many liters of water were in the jug at the start?
questions.solution: $1200 + 800 = 2000$ mL, which is 2 liters.

questions.stem: A baker bakes 8 cakes, one after another. Each cake takes 45 minutes. How many hours does the baking take in all?
questions.solution: $8 \times 45 = 360$ minutes, and $360 \div 60 = 6$ hours.

questions.stem: Which length of time is NOT the same as 2 hours 20 minutes?
questions.solution: 2 hours 20 minutes is 140 minutes. 1 hour 80 minutes is 60 + 80 = 140 and 120 + 20 = 140, but 2 hours 2 minutes is only 122 minutes.

questions.stem: A hose fills one tub every 15 minutes. How many tubs does it fill in 3 hours?
questions.solution: 3 hours is 180 minutes. $180 \div 15 = 12$ tubs.

questions.stem: Add 1 hour 50 minutes and 2 hours 40 minutes. How many minutes is the total?
questions.solution: 1 hour 50 minutes is 110 minutes and 2 hours 40 minutes is 160 minutes. $110 + 160 = 270$ minutes.

questions.stem: A cake goes into the oven at 10:35 in the morning and comes out at 1:05 in the afternoon. For how many minutes was it baking?
questions.solution: 10:35 to 12:35 is 120 minutes, then 12:35 to 1:05 is 30 minutes. $120 + 30 = 150$ minutes.

questions.stem: Kai started his chores at 3:50 PM. He washed dishes for 25 minutes and then worked in the yard for 40 minutes. At what time did he finish?
questions.solution: 25 + 40 = 65 minutes, which is 1 hour 5 minutes. 3:50 plus 1 hour is 4:50, plus 5 minutes is 4:55 PM.

questions.stem: A school day has 5 classes of 50 minutes each. There is a 10 minute break between classes, so 4 breaks in all. How many minutes pass from the start of the first class to the end of the last class?
questions.solution: Classes: $5 \times 50 = 250$ minutes. Breaks: $4 \times 10 = 40$ minutes. $250 + 40 = 290$ minutes.

questions.stem: A trip leaves at 9:20 in the morning and takes 3 hours 55 minutes. At what time does it arrive?
questions.solution: 9:20 plus 3 hours is 12:20. Plus 40 minutes is 1:00, plus the last 15 minutes is 1:15 PM.

questions.stem: A show that lasted 1 hour 50 minutes ended at 4:05. It started between 2:00 and 3:00. How many minutes after 2:00 did it start?
questions.solution: Going back 1 hour 50 minutes from 4:05: back 1 hour is 3:05, back 50 more minutes is 2:15. So it started at 2:15.

solve.work: 4:05 - 1 h 50 min = 2:15, which is between 2:00 and 3:00; 15 minutes after 2:00.

questions.stem: A bus comes at 7:00 and then every 20 minutes after that. How many hours after 7:00 does the 7th bus come? (The bus at 7:00 is the 1st bus.)
questions.solution: The 7th bus is 6 gaps after the 1st. $6 \times 20 = 120$ minutes, which is 2 hours.

solve.work: 7th bus is 6 intervals after the 1st: 6 x 20 = 120 min = 2 hours.

questions.stem: Ana studies from 4:15 to 5:05. Ben studies from 4:40 to 6:00. How many more minutes does Ben study than Ana?
questions.solution: Ana studies 50 minutes. Ben studies 80 minutes. $80 - 50 = 30$ minutes.

questions.stem: A ribbon is 3 feet 4 inches long. It is cut into 4 equal pieces. How many inches long is each piece?
questions.solution: 3 feet 4 inches is 40 inches. $40 \div 4 = 10$ inches.

questions.stem: A tap drips 5 mL of water every minute. How many minutes does it take to drip 1 liter?
questions.solution: 1 liter is 1000 mL. $1000 \div 5 = 200$ minutes.

questions.stem: A bag holds 2 kilograms of sand. Each pail takes 250 grams of sand. How many pails can be filled completely?
questions.solution: 2 kilograms is 2000 grams. $2000 \div 250 = 8$ pails.

questions.stem: Tom is 5 feet tall. His sister is 14 inches shorter than Tom. How many inches tall is his sister?
questions.solution: Tom is 60 inches tall. $60 - 14 = 46$ inches.

questions.stem: Which list shows these lengths in order from shortest to longest?
choices: 2 feet 8 inches, 30 inches, 3 feet 1 inch, 4 feet
30 inches, 3 feet 1 inch, 2 feet 8 inches, 4 feet
4 feet, 3 feet 1 inch, 2 feet 8 inches, 30 inches
30 inches, 2 feet 8 inches, 3 feet 1 inch, 4 feet
questions.answer: 30 inches, 2 feet 8 inches, 3 feet 1 inch, 4 feet
questions.solution: In inches: 30, 32, 37 and 48. So the order is 30 inches, 2 feet 8 inches, 3 feet 1 inch, 4 feet.

solve.answer: 30 inches, 2 feet 8 inches, 3 feet 1 inch, 4 feet

questions.stem: Every day for 4 days, a runner jogs for 45 minutes in the morning and 1 hour 30 minutes in the evening. How many hours does the runner jog in all?
questions.solution: Each day: $45 + 90 = 135$ minutes. For 4 days: $4 \times 135 = 540$ minutes, which is $540 \div 60 = 9$ hours.

solve.work: 45 + 90 = 135 min a day; 4 x 135 = 540 min = 9 hours.

questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. Ana eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza did she eat?
questions.solution: The pizza has 4 equal slices and Ana ate 1 of them, so she ate $\frac{1}{4}$.

questions.stem: A ribbon is cut into 6 equal pieces. What fraction of the ribbon is one piece?
questions.solution: One of 6 equal pieces is $\frac{1}{6}$ of the ribbon.

questions.stem: Which of these is a unit fraction?
questions.solution: A unit fraction has 1 on top. Only $\frac{1}{7}$ has a numerator of 1.

questions.stem: A chocolate bar has 8 equal squares. Each square is $\frac{1}{?}$ of the bar. What number replaces the ?
questions.solution: The bar is cut into 8 equal squares, so each is $\frac{1}{8}$ of it. The missing number is 8.

questions.stem: Which of these fractions is the largest?
questions.solution: When the top is 1, cutting into fewer pieces makes bigger pieces. Halves are the biggest of these.

solve.work: Among unit fractions, the smallest denominator is largest: 1/2.

questions.stem: Jake cuts a sandwich into 2 equal pieces and eats one of them. What fraction of the sandwich did Jake eat?
questions.solution: One of 2 equal pieces is $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Pablo eats 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza did he eat?
questions.solution: 3 of the 8 equal slices is $\frac{3}{8}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A chocolate bar has 10 equal squares. Seven squares are left. What fraction of the bar is left?
questions.solution: 7 of the 10 equal squares are left: $\frac{7}{10}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A fence has 5 equal sections. Two sections are painted blue. What fraction of the fence is blue?
questions.solution: 2 of the 5 equal sections: $\frac{2}{5}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: Which fraction means 3 out of 4 equal parts?
questions.solution: The bottom number tells how many equal parts, 4. The top number tells how many are taken, 3. That is $\frac{3}{4}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A pie is cut into 6 equal slices. Two slices are eaten. What fraction of the pie is left?
questions.solution: 6 - 2 = 4 slices are left out of 6: $\frac{4}{6}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to one whole?
questions.solution: A whole is all of the equal parts. All 6 of 6 parts is $\frac{6}{6}$.

questions.stem: There are 10 apples in a bag. Three of them are red. What fraction of the apples are red?
questions.solution: 3 of the 10 apples: $\frac{3}{10}$.

questions.stem: Mia has 16 stickers and gives half of them to her brother. How many stickers does she give away?
questions.solution: Half of 16 is $16 \div 2 = 8$.

questions.stem: What is $\frac{1}{3}$ of 12?
questions.solution: Split 12 into 3 equal groups: $12 \div 3 = 4$.

questions.stem: In a class of 20 students, $\frac{1}{4}$ of the students walk to school. How many students walk?
questions.solution: $20 \div 4 = 5$ students.

questions.stem: A box has 6 crayons and 2 of them are blue. What fraction of the crayons are NOT blue?
questions.solution: $6 - 2 = 4$ crayons are not blue, out of 6: $\frac{4}{6}$.

questions.stem: Which number is $\frac{1}{5}$ of 20?
There are 5 stars in a row. Four of them are gold. What fraction of the stars are gold?
questions.solution: 4 of the 5 stars: $\frac{4}{5}$.

questions.stem: Find the missing number: $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{?}{8}$. What number replaces the ?
questions.solution: Cut each half into 4 equal pieces to get 8 pieces in all, so 1 half is 4 eighths: $\frac{1}{2}$ = $\frac{4}{8}$.

questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to one half?
questions.solution: 3 out of 6 equal parts is half of the whole, so $\frac{3}{6}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices and Ben eats 2 of them. A same-size pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. How many of those slices make the same amount?
questions.solution: Each fourth is 2 eighths, so 2 fourths is 4 eighths.

questions.stem: Which pair of fractions is equal?
questions.solution: Doubling both the top and bottom of $\frac{1}{3}$ gives $\frac{2}{6}$, which is the same amount.

questions.stem: A bar is cut into 5 equal parts. Then every part is cut in half, so there are 10 equal pieces. One of the first 5 parts is the same as how many of the small pieces?
questions.solution: Each of the 5 parts is cut into 2 pieces, so $\frac{1}{5}$ = $\frac{2}{10}$.

solve.work: Each fifth is cut into 2 tenths: 2.

questions.stem: Which fraction is the greatest?
questions.solution: The bottoms are all 8, so the one with the most eighths is the greatest: $\frac{5}{8}$.

questions.stem: Which fraction is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{3}{4}$ is 3 of 4 equal parts, which is more than half. The others are all less than half.

questions.stem: Mia ate $\frac{2}{5}$ of a cake and Zoe ate $\frac{4}{5}$ of the same cake. How many more fifths did Zoe eat than Mia?
questions.solution: $4 - 2 = 2$ fifths.

questions.stem: Compare $\frac{2}{5}$ and $\frac{4}{5}$. Which is true?
questions.solution: Both are fifths, and 2 fifths is fewer than 4 fifths.

questions.stem: Ana ate $\frac{1}{3}$ of a pizza and Ben ate $\frac{1}{5}$ of a pizza of the same size. Who ate more?
questions.solution: Thirds are bigger pieces than fifths, so $\frac{1}{3}$ is more than $\frac{1}{5}$.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: Between which two whole numbers is $\frac{7}{4}$?
questions.solution: 4 fourths make 1 whole and 8 fourths make 2 wholes. 7 fourths is between them.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: $\frac{3}{4}$ is between 0 and which whole number?
questions.solution: $\frac{3}{4}$ is less than $\frac{4}{4}$ = 1, so it lies between 0 and 1.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: Which of these fractions is between 0 and 1?
questions.solution: A fraction is less than 1 when its top is less than its bottom. Only $\frac{2}{5}$ qualifies.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: Each pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. How many whole pizzas can be made from 8 slices?
Sam shares 20 marbles equally among 5 friends. What fraction of all the marbles does each friend get?
questions.solution: 5 friends share equally, so each gets 1 of 5 equal shares: $\frac{1}{5}$.

questions.stem: Mia eats $\frac{1}{8}$ of a pie each day. How many days does it take her to eat the whole pie?
questions.solution: Eight pieces of $\frac{1}{8}$ make 1 whole, so it takes 8 days.

questions.stem: Which statement is true?
choices: A pizza cut into 5 equal slices has slices that are each $\frac{1}{5}$ of the pizza.
A pizza cut into 5 slices of different sizes has slices that are each $\frac{1}{5}$ of the pizza.
A pizza cut into 5 equal slices has slices that are each $\frac{1}{4}$ of the pizza.
A pizza cut into 5 equal slices has slices that are each 5 of the pizza.
questions.answer: A pizza cut into 5 equal slices has slices that are each $\frac{1}{5}$ of the pizza.
questions.solution: A unit fraction needs EQUAL parts. 5 equal slices make fifths, so each slice is $\frac{1}{5}$.

solve.answer: A pizza cut into 5 equal slices has slices that are each $\frac{1}{5}$ of the pizza.
solve.work: Equal slices, 5 of them: each 1/5. The unequal-slices statement is false.

questions.stem: Which list puts these fractions in order from the smallest to the largest?
questions.solution: More pieces means smaller pieces. Ninths are the smallest, then sixths, thirds and halves.

questions.stem: I am a unit fraction. My denominator is the number of days in one week. What fraction am I? (Write it as a fraction.)
questions.solution: A unit fraction has numerator 1. A week has 7 days, so I am $\frac{1}{7}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A flag has 12 equal stripes. Five are red, 4 are white and the rest are blue. What fraction of the flag is blue?
questions.solution: $5 + 4 = 9$ stripes are red or white, so $12 - 9 = 3$ are blue: $\frac{3}{12}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A tray has 8 equal brownies. Five of them are eaten. What fraction of the brownies is NOT eaten?
questions.solution: $8 - 5 = 3$ brownies are left out of 8: $\frac{3}{8}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A rectangle is cut into 9 equal parts and 4 parts are shaded. How many more parts must be shaded so that $\frac{7}{9}$ of the rectangle is shaded?
questions.solution: $\frac{7}{9}$ means 7 shaded parts. $7 - 4 = 3$ more parts.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A pizza has 8 equal slices. Rae eats 3 slices, Tim eats 2 slices and Bo eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza is left?
questions.solution: $3 + 2 + 1 = 6$ slices are eaten, so $8 - 6 = 2$ slices are left: $\frac{2}{8}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: Which sentence tells what $\frac{5}{8}$ means?
choices: The whole is cut into 8 equal parts and 5 of them are taken.
The whole is cut into 5 equal parts and 8 of them are taken.
The whole is cut into 8 parts of any size and 5 of them are taken.
The whole is cut into 8 equal parts and 8 minus 5 of them are taken.
questions.answer: The whole is cut into 8 equal parts and 5 of them are taken.
questions.solution: The bottom number says how many equal parts, 8. The top number says how many are taken, 5.

solve.answer: The whole is cut into 8 equal parts and 5 of them are taken.
solve.work: Denominator 8 = equal parts, numerator 5 = parts taken.

questions.stem: A farmer has 24 hens. $\frac{3}{8}$ of them are brown. How many hens are brown?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{8}$ of 24 is $24 \div 8 = 3$, so $\frac{3}{8}$ is $3 \times 3 = 9$ hens.

questions.stem: A bag has 18 candies. $\frac{2}{3}$ of them are red. How many candies are NOT red?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{3}$ of 18 is 6, so $\frac{2}{3}$ is 12 red candies. $18 - 12 = 6$ are not red. (Or: the not-red part is $\frac{1}{3}$ of 18, which is 6.)

questions.stem: Which number is $\frac{2}{5}$ of 30?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{5}$ of 30 is 6, so $\frac{2}{5}$ is $2 \times 6 = 12$.

questions.stem: Out of 30 students, 12 chose soccer. What fraction of the students chose soccer?
questions.solution: 12 of the 30 students: $\frac{12}{30}$.

questions.stem: A vase has 12 flowers. Five are red, 4 are yellow and the rest are pink. What fraction of the flowers are pink?
questions.solution: $5 + 4 = 9$ are red or yellow, so $12 - 9 = 3$ are pink: $\frac{3}{12}$.

questions.stem: Ella read $\frac{3}{5}$ of a 40 page book. How many pages does she still have to read?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{5}$ of 40 is 8, so $\frac{3}{5}$ is 24 pages read. $40 - 24 = 16$ pages are left.

questions.stem: $\frac{3}{4} = \frac{?}{12}$. What number goes in place of the ?
questions.solution: The bottom went from 4 to 12, multiplying by 3. Do the same to the top: $3 \times 3 = 9$.

questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to $\frac{2}{3}$?
questions.solution: Multiply the top and bottom by 2: $\frac{2}{3}$ = $\frac{4}{6}$.

questions.stem: Kate colored 6 of the 8 equal squares on a card. If the same card had been cut into 4 equal squares, how many would be colored?
questions.solution: Pairs of small squares make one big square, so $6 \div 2 = 3$ big squares: $\frac{6}{8}$ = $\frac{3}{4}$.

questions.stem: Which fraction is NOT equal to $\frac{1}{2}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{5}{10}$, $\frac{4}{8}$ and $\frac{3}{6}$ are all half. $\frac{4}{6}$ is two thirds.

questions.stem: Two thirds of a ribbon is cut off. How many twelfths of the ribbon is that?
questions.solution: Thirds to twelfths: multiply the bottom by 4, so multiply the top by 4 too: $\frac{2}{3}$ = $\frac{8}{12}$.

questions.stem: Maya says $\frac{2}{5}$ = $\frac{4}{10}$. Dan says $\frac{2}{5}$ = $\frac{4}{7}$. Who is right?
questions.solution: Doubling the top and bottom of $\frac{2}{5}$ gives $\frac{4}{10}$, so Maya is right. For $\frac{4}{7}$ the bottom would have to go from 5 to 7 by adding 2, but equal fractions come from multiplying both numbers by the same amount, so Dan is wrong.

questions.stem: Two bars are the same size. The first bar is cut into 3 equal parts and 2 parts are colored. The second bar is cut into 5 equal parts and 2 parts are colored. Which bar has more colored?
questions.solution: Compare $\frac{2}{3}$ and $\frac{2}{5}$. Thirds are bigger than fifths, so 2 thirds is more than 2 fifths.

questions.stem: How many of these fractions are greater than $\frac{1}{2}$: $\frac{3}{8}$, $\frac{5}{6}$, $\frac{4}{10}$, $\frac{7}{12}$, $\frac{1}{3}$, $\frac{2}{3}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{5}{6}$, $\frac{7}{12}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$ are each more than half. The others are less than half.

questions.stem: Which list shows these fractions from the smallest to the largest?
Which whole number can replace the ? so that $\frac{?}{6}$ is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$ but less than $\frac{5}{6}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{2}$ is $\frac{3}{6}$ and the number must be more than 3 but less than 5. Only 4 fits.

questions.stem: Kim and Lou have ribbons of the same length. Kim used $\frac{3}{4}$ of her ribbon and Lou used $\frac{5}{8}$ of his. Who used more?
questions.solution: $\frac{3}{4}$ = $\frac{6}{8}$, which is more than $\frac{5}{8}$. Kim used more.

questions.stem: How many fractions with a bottom number of 8 are greater than $\frac{1}{8}$ and less than $\frac{5}{8}$?
questions.solution: They are $\frac{2}{8}$, $\frac{3}{8}$ and $\frac{4}{8}$: 3 fractions.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: $\frac{9}{4}$ is between 2 and which whole number?
questions.solution: $\frac{8}{4}$ = 2 and $\frac{12}{4}$ = 3, so $\frac{9}{4}$ is between 2 and 3.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: Which fraction is between 2 and 3?
questions.solution: 3 thirds make 1, so 6 thirds make 2 and 9 thirds make 3. $\frac{7}{3}$ is between 6 and 9 thirds.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: Pam has 11 pieces of pizza. Each piece is $\frac{1}{3}$ of a pizza. How many whole pizzas can she make from the pieces?
questions.solution: Every 3 pieces make 1 pizza. $11 \div 3$ is 3 with 2 left over, so she can make 3 whole pizzas.

solve.work: 11 thirds = 3 wholes and 2 thirds: 3 whole pizzas.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: Mara says $\frac{9}{5}$ is more than 2. What is the best reply?
questions.solution: 5 fifths make 1 and 10 fifths make 2. 9 fifths is between 5 and 10 fifths, so it lies between 1 and 2.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: How many halves are there in 3 whole pies?
questions.solution: Each pie has 2 halves, so $3 \times 2 = 6$ halves.

questions.stem: A unit fraction is smaller than $\frac{1}{6}$ but larger than $\frac{1}{8}$. What is its denominator?
questions.solution: Bigger denominators make smaller unit fractions, so the denominator is between 6 and 8. It is 7.

questions.stem: Four friends cut identical sandwiches into equal pieces. Ava cuts hers into 6 pieces, Ben into 9, Cy into 4 and Di into 12. Whose pieces are the biggest?
questions.solution: Fewer pieces means each piece is bigger. Cy cut into only 4 pieces, so each of Cy's pieces is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the sandwich, the biggest.

solve.work: Fewest pieces of the same sandwich are biggest: Cy (4 pieces).

questions.stem: $\frac{1}{4}$ of the marbles in a jar is 6 marbles. How many marbles are in the jar?
questions.solution: 6 marbles are one of 4 equal parts, so the jar has $4 \times 6 = 24$ marbles.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: Mia cuts $\frac{2}{10}$ of a ribbon off, then $\frac{3}{10}$ of the ribbon, then $\frac{1}{10}$ of the ribbon. What fraction of the ribbon is left?
questions.solution: She cut off $2 + 3 + 1 = 6$ tenths, so $10 - 6 = 4$ tenths are left: $\frac{4}{10}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: Seven of the 9 equal parts of a field are planted with corn. The corn covers 28 square meters. How many square meters is the whole field?
questions.solution: 7 parts cover 28 square meters, so 1 part covers $28 \div 7 = 4$. All 9 parts: $9 \times 4 = 36$ square meters.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A candy bar has 12 equal pieces. Lee eats 4 pieces and Mia eats 3 pieces. What fraction of the candy bar is left?
questions.solution: $4 + 3 = 7$ pieces are eaten, so $12 - 7 = 5$ are left: $\frac{5}{12}$.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Then every slice is cut in half, making smaller slices that are all equal. Ana eats 5 of the smaller slices. What fraction of the whole pizza did she eat?
questions.solution: Cutting each of 8 slices in half makes $8 \times 2 = 16$ equal slices. Ana ate 5 of them: $\frac{5}{16}$.

solve.work: 8 slices halved = 16 equal slices; 5 of them = 5/16.

questions.skill: Naming a fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 12 equal slices. Ann eats 3 slices, Bo eats 4 slices and Cy eats 2 slices. Who ate exactly $\frac{1}{3}$ of the pizza?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{3}$ of 12 slices is 4 slices, and Bo ate 4. Ann ate $\frac{3}{12}$ (one fourth) and Cy ate $\frac{2}{12}$ (one sixth).

questions.stem: $\frac{3}{8}$ of the passengers on a bus are children. There are 15 children. How many passengers are on the bus?
questions.solution: 3 parts are 15 children, so 1 part is $15 \div 3 = 5$. All 8 parts: $8 \times 5 = 40$ passengers.

questions.stem: A class has 24 students. $\frac{1}{3}$ of them wear glasses and $\frac{1}{4}$ of them are left-handed. No student does both. How many students are neither left-handed nor wearing glasses?
questions.solution: Glasses: $24 \div 3 = 8$. Left-handed: $24 \div 4 = 6$. Together 14 students, so $24 - 14 = 10$ are neither.

questions.stem: Which of these is the greatest?
questions.solution: $\frac{2}{3}$ of 12 is 8, $\frac{3}{4}$ of 12 is 9, $\frac{1}{2}$ of 14 is 7, and $\frac{5}{6}$ of 12 is 10. The greatest is 10.

questions.stem: A jar has 40 marbles. Half of them are blue. Then $\frac{1}{4}$ of the marbles that are NOT blue are green. How many green marbles are there?
questions.solution: Not blue: $40 \div 2 = 20$ marbles. One fourth of 20 is $20 \div 4 = 5$ green marbles.

questions.stem: Mai had 45 dollars. She spent $\frac{2}{3}$ of it on a book and $\frac{1}{5}$ of it on lunch. How many dollars does she have left?
questions.solution: Book: $45 \div 3 \times 2 = 30$ dollars. Lunch: $45 \div 5 = 9$ dollars. $45 - 30 - 9 = 6$ dollars are left.

questions.stem: In a box of marbles, half are red and $\frac{1}{3}$ are blue. The other 5 marbles are green. How many marbles are in the box?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{2}$ + $\frac{1}{3}$ = $\frac{5}{6}$ of the marbles are red or blue (sixths: 3 + 2 = 5). So the 5 green marbles are $\frac{1}{6}$ of the box, and the box has $6 \times 5 = 30$ marbles.

questions.stem: Only one of these statements is true. Which one?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{4}$ of 20 is 5 and $\frac{1}{5}$ of 25 is 5. In the others the two amounts are 5 and 4, 5 and 4, 6 and 4.

solve.work: 5 vs 4; 5 vs 4; 6 vs 4; 5 vs 5. Only the last is true.

questions.stem: Tara has run $\frac{3}{5}$ of a race. If the race were cut into 25 equal parts, how many parts would she have run?
questions.solution: 5 times 5 is 25, so multiply the top by 5 too: $3 \times 5 = 15$.

questions.stem: $\frac{4}{?} = \frac{12}{18}$. Which number is hiding behind the ?
questions.solution: $\frac{12}{18}$ divided top and bottom by 3 is $\frac{4}{6}$. The missing number is 6.

questions.stem: Three of these four fractions are equal to each other. Which fraction is the odd one out?
questions.solution: $\frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{4}{6}$ and $\frac{6}{9}$ are all two thirds. $\frac{8}{10}$ is four fifths.

questions.stem: A fraction is equal to $\frac{1}{2}$. Its top number and bottom number add up to 12. What is its bottom number?
questions.solution: Halves have a bottom number twice the top. Top + bottom = 12 means the top is 4 and the bottom is 8: $\frac{4}{8}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.stem: What is $\frac{12}{16}$ written in its simplest form?
questions.solution: Divide the top and bottom by 4: $\frac{12}{16}$ = $\frac{3}{4}$. $\frac{6}{8}$ is equal too, but can still be made simpler.

questions.stem: An hour has 60 minutes. 45 minutes is $\frac{45}{60}$ of an hour. Written as twelfths, the top number would be what?
questions.solution: Divide the top and bottom by 5: $\frac{45}{60}$ = $\frac{9}{12}$.

questions.stem: Which of these fractions is the greatest?
questions.solution: In twelfths: $\frac{9}{12}$, $\frac{8}{12}$, $\frac{7}{12}$ and $\frac{10}{12}$. The greatest is $\frac{5}{6}$.

questions.stem: Put these four fractions in order, smallest first. Which list is right?
questions.solution: In eighths: $\frac{3}{8}$, $\frac{4}{8}$, $\frac{5}{8}$, $\frac{6}{8}$. That is the order shown.

questions.stem: A fraction with a bottom number of 8 is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$ and less than $\frac{3}{4}$. What is the fraction?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{2}$ = $\frac{4}{8}$ and $\frac{3}{4}$ = $\frac{6}{8}$. The only eighth between them is $\frac{5}{8}$.

questions.stem: Which comparison is true?
questions.solution: With the same top number, the larger bottom number makes the smaller fraction. 9 is more than 7, so $\frac{4}{9}$ is less than $\frac{4}{7}$.

solve.work: Same numerator, smaller denominator larger: 4/9 < 4/7 true; others false.

questions.stem: Ann ate $\frac{5}{6}$ of a cake, Bo ate $\frac{2}{3}$ of an equal cake and Cy ate $\frac{3}{4}$ of another equal cake. How many twelfths more did Ann eat than Bo?
questions.solution: $\frac{5}{6}$ = $\frac{10}{12}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$ = $\frac{8}{12}$. The difference is $10 - 8 = 2$ twelfths.

questions.stem: Which fraction is the closest to 1 whole?
questions.solution: Each is short of 1 by one unit fraction: $\frac{1}{10}$, $\frac{1}{8}$, $\frac{1}{6}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$. The smallest gap is $\frac{1}{10}$, so $\frac{9}{10}$ is the closest.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: How many fractions with a bottom number of 4 are greater than 1 and less than 2?
questions.solution: 1 is $\frac{4}{4}$ and 2 is $\frac{8}{4}$. The fractions between are $\frac{5}{4}$, $\frac{6}{4}$ and $\frac{7}{4}$: 3 fractions.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: Which list has only fractions that lie between 1 and 2?
questions.solution: Between 1 and 2 means more than $\frac{4}{4}$ and less than $\frac{8}{4}$. In the first list all three do. $\frac{4}{4}$ equals 1, $\frac{5}{2}$ is more than 2 and $\frac{1}{2}$ is less than 1.

solve.work: 5/4, 3/2, 7/4 all between 1 and 2; other lists contain 1/2, 4/4 (=1) or 5/2.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: A fraction with a bottom number of 5 is between 2 and 3 and its top number is a multiple of 4. What is the fraction?
questions.solution: 2 is $\frac{10}{5}$ and 3 is $\frac{15}{5}$, so the top is 11, 12, 13 or 14. The only multiple of 4 is 12: $\frac{12}{5}$.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: The fraction $\frac{23}{6}$ lies between two neighboring whole numbers. What is the sum of those two whole numbers?
questions.solution: $\frac{18}{6}$ = 3 and $\frac{24}{6}$ = 4. $\frac{23}{6}$ lies between 3 and 4, and $3 + 4 = 7$.

questions.skill: Where a fraction lies between whole numbers
questions.stem: Which fraction is greater than 3 and less than $\frac{7}{2}$?
questions.solution: 3 is $\frac{12}{4}$ and $\frac{7}{2}$ is $\frac{14}{4}$. The only fraction between them is $\frac{13}{4}$.

questions.stem: Round $47$ to the nearest 10.
questions.solution: $47$ lies between $40$ and $50$. It is closer to $50$, so it rounds to $50$.

questions.stem: A bag holds 83 marbles. To the nearest 10, about how many marbles is that?
questions.solution: $83$ lies between $80$ and $90$. It is closer to $80$, so it rounds to $80$.

questions.stem: A path is 91 meters long. How long is the path to the nearest 10 meters?
questions.solution: $91$ lies between $90$ and $100$. It is closer to $90$, so it rounds to $90$.

questions.stem: Which number is $26$ rounded to the nearest ten?
questions.solution: $26$ lies between $20$ and $30$. It is closer to $30$, so it rounds to $30$.

questions.stem: Round $284$ to the nearest 100.
questions.solution: $284$ lies between $200$ and $300$. It is closer to $300$, so it rounds to $300$.

questions.stem: A school has 619 students. To the nearest 100, about how many students does it have?
questions.solution: $619$ lies between $600$ and $700$. It is closer to $600$, so it rounds to $600$.

questions.stem: A trail is 342 meters long. Round its length to the nearest 100 meters.
questions.solution: $342$ lies between $300$ and $400$. It is closer to $300$, so it rounds to $300$.

questions.stem: Which number is $871$ rounded to the nearest hundred?
questions.solution: $871$ lies between $800$ and $900$. It is closer to $900$, so it rounds to $900$.

questions.stem: A website had 4,380 visitors in a month. How many is that to the nearest 1,000?
questions.solution: $4{,}380$ lies between $4{,}000$ and $5{,}000$. It is closer to $4{,}000$, so it rounds to $4{,}000$.

questions.stem: A stadium has 7,640 seats. Round the number of seats to the nearest thousand.
questions.solution: $7{,}640$ lies between $7{,}000$ and $8{,}000$. It is closer to $8{,}000$, so it rounds to $8{,}000$.

questions.stem: A jar holds 2,815 beans. Round the number of beans to the nearest 1,000.
questions.solution: $2{,}815$ lies between $2{,}000$ and $3{,}000$. It is closer to $3{,}000$, so it rounds to $3{,}000$.

questions.stem: Which number is $5{,}490$ rounded to the nearest 1,000?
questions.solution: $5{,}490$ lies between $5{,}000$ and $6{,}000$. It is closer to $5{,}000$, so it rounds to $5{,}000$.

questions.skill: Which numbers round to a given number
questions.stem: Which of these numbers rounds to 50 when rounded to the nearest 10?
questions.solution: 46 is closer to 50 than to 40, so it rounds to 50. 44 rounds to 40, 56 rounds to 60 and 39 rounds to 40.

questions.skill: Which numbers round to a given number
questions.stem: Which number rounds to 300 when rounded to the nearest hundred?
questions.solution: 349 is between 300 and 400 and is closer to 300. 360 and 420 round to 400, and 240 rounds to 200.

questions.skill: Which numbers round to a given number
questions.stem: Look at these numbers: 14, 17, 21, 26, 24. How many of them round to 20 when rounded to the nearest 10?
questions.solution: 17, 21 and 24 round to 20. 14 rounds to 10 and 26 rounds to 30. So 3 numbers round to 20.

questions.stem: Estimate 38 + 41 by rounding each number to the nearest 10 first.
questions.solution: 38 rounds to 40 and 41 rounds to 40. Then 40 + 40 = 80.

questions.stem: Ana has 52 red beads and 29 blue beads. She rounds each number to the nearest 10 to estimate how many beads she has in all. What is her estimate?
questions.solution: 52 rounds to 50 and 29 rounds to 30. Then 50 + 30 = 80.

questions.stem: Estimate 71 - 29 by rounding each number to the nearest 10 first.
questions.solution: 71 rounds to 70 and 29 rounds to 30. Then 70 - 30 = 40.

questions.stem: A book has 98 pages. Lee has read 52 of them. Round each number to the nearest 10 to estimate how many pages Lee has left to read.
questions.solution: 98 rounds to 100 and 52 rounds to 50. Then 100 - 50 = 50.

questions.stem: Estimate 197 + 104 by rounding each number to the nearest 100 first.
questions.solution: 197 rounds to 200 and 104 rounds to 100. Then 200 + 100 = 300.

questions.stem: Estimate 403 - 198 by rounding each number to the nearest 100 first.
questions.solution: 403 rounds to 400 and 198 rounds to 200. Then 400 - 200 = 200.

questions.stem: Estimate $29 \times 3$ by rounding 29 to the nearest 10 first.
questions.solution: 29 rounds to 30. Then 30 times 3 is 90.

questions.stem: A box holds 18 pencils. Round 18 to the nearest 10 to estimate how many pencils are in 4 boxes.
questions.solution: 18 rounds to 20. Then 20 times 4 is 80.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 10 centimeters by 8 centimeters. A square with 3-centimeter sides is cut out of one corner. What is the area that is left?
questions.solution: The rectangle has area 10 times 8 = 80. The square has area 9. Left: 80 - 9 = 71 square centimeters.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: A yard is 14 meters long and 10 meters wide. A pond in the yard is 4 meters by 5 meters. The rest of the yard is grass. What is the area of the grass, in square meters?
questions.solution: The yard has area 140. The pond has area 20. Grass: 140 - 20 = 120 square meters.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangle that is 12 meters long and 9 meters wide is cut into two rectangles by one straight cut. One piece is 12 meters by 4 meters. What is the area of the other piece?
questions.solution: The other piece is 12 meters by 9 - 4 = 5 meters. Its area is 12 times 5 = 60 square meters.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: Three rectangles that do not overlap are joined to make one shape. Their sizes are 6 by 2, 5 by 3 and 4 by 4, all in centimeters. What is the area of the shape, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: 6 times 2 = 12, 5 times 3 = 15 and 4 times 4 = 16. Together: 12 + 15 + 16 = 43 square centimeters.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: An L-shaped room is made from a 7-meter by 6-meter rectangle and a 4-meter by 2-meter rectangle that do not overlap. What is the area of the room?
questions.solution: 7 times 6 = 42 and 4 times 2 = 8. Together: 42 + 8 = 50 square meters.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 13 meters long and 9 meters wide. What is its perimeter, in meters?
questions.solution: Perimeter = 13 + 9 + 13 + 9 = 44 meters.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 18 centimeters and a width of 4 centimeters. How long is the rectangle?
questions.solution: Length plus width is half the perimeter: 18 divided by 2 = 9. So the length is 9 - 4 = 5 centimeters.

questions.stem: A square has sides of 6 centimeters. A rectangle is 4 centimeters by 9 centimeters. Which sentence is true?
choices: They have the same area, but different perimeters.
They have the same perimeter, but different areas.
They have the same area and the same perimeter.
They have different areas and different perimeters.
questions.answer: They have the same area, but different perimeters.
questions.solution: Both areas are 36 square centimeters. The perimeters are 24 and 26 centimeters, which are different.

solve.answer: They have the same area, but different perimeters.
solve.work: Square: area 36, perimeter 24. Rectangle: area 36, perimeter 26.

questions.stem: A square park has a perimeter of 52 meters. How long is each side, in meters?
questions.solution: A square has 4 equal sides, so each side is 52 divided by 4 = 13 meters.

questions.stem: Four rectangles each have an area of 24 square units. Which one has the greatest perimeter?
questions.solution: The perimeters are 50, 28, 22 and 20 units. The long, thin rectangle has the greatest.

questions.stem: A fence goes around a garden that is 12 meters long and 7 meters wide. Each meter of fence costs 5 dollars. How many dollars does the fence cost?
questions.solution: Distance around: 12 + 7 + 12 + 7 = 38 meters. At 5 dollars each: 38 times 5 = 190 dollars.

questions.stem: A floor is 12 feet by 9 feet. Square tiles each cover 1 square foot and cost 2 dollars each. How many dollars do the tiles for the floor cost?
questions.solution: The floor has area 12 times 9 = 108 square feet, so it needs 108 tiles. 108 times 2 = 216 dollars.

questions.stem: How many different rectangles with whole-number sides have an area of 18 square units? A 3 by 6 and a 6 by 3 count as the same rectangle.
questions.solution: The pairs that multiply to 18 are 1 by 18, 2 by 9 and 3 by 6. That is 3 rectangles.

questions.stem: A rug that is 5 meters by 4 meters lies on a floor that is 8 meters by 6 meters. How many square meters of the floor are not covered?
questions.solution: The floor has area 48 and the rug has area 20. Not covered: 48 - 20 = 28 square meters.

questions.stem: One liter of paint covers 10 square meters. A wall is 8 meters long and 5 meters tall. How many liters are needed to paint the whole wall once?
questions.solution: The wall has area 8 times 5 = 40 square meters. 40 divided by 10 = 4 liters.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 9 centimeters wide. Its length is 4 centimeters more than its width. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The length is 9 + 4 = 13 centimeters. Area = 9 times 13 = 117 square centimeters.

questions.stem: A rectangular field is 25 meters by 48 meters. What is its area, in square meters? (Hint: 25 times 4 is easy.)
questions.solution: 25 times 48 = 25 times 4 times 12 = 100 times 12 = 1,200 square meters.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 9 meters by 14 meters. Its width is doubled to 18 meters and its length stays the same. What is the new area?
questions.solution: New area = 18 times 14 = 252 square meters. (It is double the old area of 126.)

questions.stem: A rectangle is 4 centimeters by 5 centimeters. Another rectangle has sides 3 times as long: 12 centimeters by 15 centimeters. The second area is how many times the first area?
questions.solution: The first area is 4 times 5 = 20. The second is 12 times 15 = 180. 180 divided by 20 = 9 times as large.

questions.skill: Finding a missing side from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 156 square meters and a width of 12 meters. How long is it, in meters?
questions.solution: Length = 156 divided by 12 = 13 meters.

questions.skill: Finding a missing side from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 144 square centimeters. Its length is 4 times its width. How wide is the rectangle?
questions.solution: Try widths: 6 wide gives length 24, and 6 times 24 = 144. So the width is 6 centimeters.

solve.work: w x 4w = 144, w x w = 36, w = 6 (length 24).

questions.skill: Finding a missing side from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 meters and a length of 9 meters. What is its area, in square meters?
questions.solution: Length plus width = 30 divided by 2 = 15, so the width is 15 - 9 = 6. Area = 9 times 6 = 54 square meters.

questions.skill: Finding a missing side from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 40 square centimeters and a perimeter of 26 centimeters. Its length is greater than its width. How long is it?
questions.solution: Length plus width = 26 divided by 2 = 13. Two numbers with sum 13 and product 40 are 8 and 5. The length is 8 centimeters.

solve.work: L + W = 13, L x W = 40: 8 and 5. Length 8.

questions.skill: Finding a missing side from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 90 square meters and a length of 15 meters. How many meters longer is its length than its width?
questions.solution: Width = 90 divided by 15 = 6 meters. The length is 15 - 6 = 9 meters longer.

questions.stem: A square has a perimeter of 36 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each side is 36 divided by 4 = 9 centimeters. Area = 9 times 9 = 81 square centimeters.

questions.stem: A square has an area of 64 square meters. What is its perimeter?
questions.solution: Each side is 8 meters, because 8 times 8 = 64. Perimeter = 4 times 8 = 32 meters.

questions.stem: One square has sides of 8 meters. Another square has sides of 5 meters. How many square meters greater is the area of the first square than the area of the second?
questions.solution: 64 - 25 = 39 square meters.

questions.stem: The sides of a square are made twice as long. How does the area change?
choices: The area becomes 2 times as large.
The area becomes 3 times as large.
The area becomes 4 times as large.
The area becomes 8 times as large.
questions.answer: The area becomes 4 times as large.
questions.solution: Try a 3 by 3 square (area 9). Doubling gives 6 by 6 (area 36), which is 4 times as large.

solve.answer: The area becomes 4 times as large.
solve.work: (2s) x (2s) = 4 x s x s: 4 times.

questions.stem: A square of paper has an area of 225 square centimeters. It is cut into 9 equal small squares, in 3 rows of 3. How long is one side of a small square, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The big square has sides of 15 centimeters, because 15 times 15 = 225. Three small squares fit across, so each side is 15 divided by 3 = 5 centimeters.

solve.work: Big side 15 (15 x 15 = 225); 3 small per side: 15 / 3 = 5.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: A picture is 20 centimeters by 15 centimeters. It sits in a frame that is 3 centimeters wide all the way around. The whole frame and picture together make a larger rectangle. What is the area of the frame itself, not counting the picture, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The larger rectangle is 20 + 6 = 26 by 15 + 6 = 21, with area 546. The picture has area 300. The frame is 546 - 300 = 246 square centimeters.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangle is 12 meters by 10 meters. A square with 4-meter sides is cut out of one corner. What is the perimeter of the shape that is left?
questions.solution: Cutting out a corner does not change the distance around: the missing top and side are replaced by two edges of the same total length. The perimeter stays 2 times (12 + 10) = 44 meters.

solve.work: Cutting a square from a corner keeps the perimeter: 2 x (12 + 10) = 44.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: A wall is 8 feet tall and 18 feet wide. It has two windows, each 3 feet by 4 feet, and one door that is 7 feet by 3 feet. The rest of the wall is painted. How many square feet are painted?
questions.solution: The wall has area 144. The windows take 2 times 12 = 24 and the door takes 21. Painted: 144 - 24 - 21 = 99 square feet.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: Three identical squares are put side by side in a row to make a rectangle with an area of 75 square centimeters. How long is the side of one square?
questions.solution: Each square has area 75 divided by 3 = 25. Since 5 times 5 = 25, each side is 5 centimeters.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangle is 16 centimeters by 9 centimeters. One straight cut makes two rectangles. One of them is 10 centimeters by 9 centimeters. What is the area of the other one, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The other piece is (16 - 10) = 6 centimeters by 9 centimeters. Area = 6 times 9 = 54 square centimeters.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: Which of these has the greatest area?
choices: A rectangle 10 meters by 8 meters with a 4-meter by 3-meter rectangle cut out of a corner
questions.solution: The areas are 81, 77, 72 and 80 - 12 = 68 square meters. The square is greatest.

questions.skill: Area of a shape made of rectangles
questions.stem: A square of 10 meters by 10 meters has an 8-meter by 3-meter rectangle cut out of one corner and a 2-meter by 2-meter square cut out of a different corner. What area is left, in square meters?
questions.solution: The big square has area 100. Take away 24 and 4: 100 - 24 - 4 = 72 square meters.

questions.stem: A rectangle has whole-number sides and a perimeter of 20 centimeters. What is the greatest area it could have, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Length plus width = 10. The pairs are 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5, with areas 9, 16, 21, 24 and 25. The greatest is 25.

solve.issues: Minor: a child who thinks a square is not a rectangle answers 24; Q96 in this set says 'A square counts as a rectangle' and this one should too.
solve.work: L + W = 10: 1x9 = 9, 2x8 = 16, 3x7 = 21, 4x6 = 24, 5x5 = 25. Greatest 25 (a square is a rectangle).

questions.stem: A fence of 20 meters goes all the way around a rectangular pen. The pen is 4 meters longer than it is wide. What is the area of the pen, in square meters?
questions.solution: Length plus width = 20 divided by 2 = 10. The length is 4 more than the width, so the sides are 7 and 3 (7 + 3 = 10 and 7 - 3 = 4). Area = 7 times 3 = 21 square meters.

questions.stem: Which pair of rectangles has the same perimeter?
choices: 3 cm by 8 cm and 4 cm by 6 cm
2 cm by 12 cm and 4 cm by 6 cm
2 cm by 8 cm and 3 cm by 6 cm
3 cm by 8 cm and 5 cm by 6 cm
questions.answer: 3 cm by 8 cm and 5 cm by 6 cm
questions.solution: The perimeters are 22 and 22 for the first pair. The other pairs have perimeters 22 and 20, 28 and 20, and 20 and 18.

solve.answer: 3 cm by 8 cm and 5 cm by 6 cm

questions.stem: A rectangle is 10 meters long and 6 meters wide. Its length is changed to 20 meters. How many meters greater is the perimeter of the new rectangle than the old one?
questions.solution: Old perimeter: 2 times 16 = 32. New perimeter: 2 times 26 = 52. 52 - 32 = 20 meters greater.

questions.stem: A square and a rectangle both have a perimeter of 36 meters. The rectangle is 12 meters long. How many square meters greater is the area of the square than the area of the rectangle?
questions.solution: The square has sides of 36 divided by 4 = 9, so its area is 81. The rectangle has width 18 - 12 = 6, so its area is 72. 81 - 72 = 9 square meters.

solve.work: Square side 9, area 81. Rectangle 12 by 6, area 72. 81 - 72 = 9.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 8 centimeters by 5 centimeters. Another rectangle has the same area and is 10 centimeters long. What is the perimeter of the second rectangle?
questions.solution: The area is 8 times 5 = 40. The second rectangle has width 40 divided by 10 = 4. Its perimeter is 10 + 4 + 10 + 4 = 28 centimeters.

questions.stem: Which sentence is true?
choices: Two rectangles with the same area must have the same perimeter.
A rectangle with a greater area must have a greater perimeter.
Two rectangles can have the same perimeter but different areas.
Two rectangles with the same perimeter must have the same area.
questions.answer: Two rectangles can have the same perimeter but different areas.
questions.solution: A 1 by 9 rectangle and a 5 by 5 rectangle both have perimeter 20, but their areas are 9 and 25. The other sentences are false for the same kind of example.

solve.answer: Two rectangles can have the same perimeter but different areas.
solve.work: E.g. 1x5 and 2x4 both have perimeter 12, areas 5 and 8.

questions.stem: How many different rectangles with whole-number sides have a perimeter of 14 centimeters? A 3 by 4 and a 4 by 3 count as the same rectangle.
questions.solution: Length plus width = 7. The pairs are 1 and 6, 2 and 5, and 3 and 4. That is 3 rectangles.

questions.stem: How many different rectangles with whole-number sides have an area of 36 square units? A square counts as a rectangle, and a 4 by 9 and a 9 by 4 count as the same rectangle.
questions.solution: The pairs that multiply to 36 are 1 by 36, 2 by 18, 3 by 12, 4 by 9 and 6 by 6. That is 5 rectangles.

questions.stem: Square tiles with 2-foot sides cover a floor that is 12 feet by 8 feet. How many tiles are needed?
questions.solution: The floor has area 96 square feet. One tile covers 2 times 2 = 4 square feet. 96 divided by 4 = 24 tiles.

solve.work: Floor 96 sq ft; tile 4 sq ft; 96 / 4 = 24 (6 by 4 tiles).

questions.stem: One can of paint covers 12 square meters. A wall is 9 meters long and 4 meters tall, and it gets 2 coats of paint. How many cans are needed?
questions.solution: One coat covers 9 times 4 = 36 square meters. Two coats cover 72 square meters. 72 divided by 12 = 6 cans.

questions.stem: Parking spaces are rectangles that are 5 meters by 2 meters. How many of them fit exactly into a parking lot that is 30 meters by 20 meters, with no gaps?
questions.solution: The lot has area 600 square meters. One space has area 10. 600 divided by 10 = 60 spaces.
